findings.failure_path: A Node.js-only schema or migration design must read either the Go or Python data-modeling reference before concluding, while lines 16 and 130 prohibit loading those stack defaults. The shared method also applies the former stacks' RPC/gRPC default to Node.js. Consequently, the named Node.js owner still directs work through defaults it explicitly forbids.
findings.smallest_fix: Condition the data-modeling references on the service's stack, provide a Node.js handoff to its implementation owner, and keep RPC defaults scoped to the stacks that establish them.

findings.failure_path: The old Go entry always exposed the external-dependency bootstrap contract: automatic resource creation, validation of existing resources, repairable partial failures, and startup-fatal failures. The replacement entry has no corresponding trigger, and this obligation sits under Architecture defaults rather than Step 4, which the new loading instructions tell a runtime-design reader to consult. A reader following that prescribed path can approve bootstrap design without considering resource mutation or partial-failure recovery.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a bootstrap-contract bullet to the entry's runtime step and place or explicitly reference the full obligation in Step 4.

findings.failure_path: The source map labels 'Durable side effects need atomic outbox evidence' as confirmed, but its justification only establishes idempotent consumption when an outbox relay republishes messages. It also removes the actual rule's atomic audit and explicit reconciliation/repair alternatives. Maintainers using this provenance can incorrectly treat outbox adoption as mandatory for every durable side effect.
findings.smallest_fix: Scope the source support to transactional state-plus-message publication and duplicate delivery; preserve the rule's audit/repair alternatives and distinguish local policy from source-supported claims.
